pointers.sentence: `modelformset_factory` makes a model form class with `modelform_factory`, then a formset class of that form with `formset_factory`, on `BaseModelFormSet`, and sets `BaseModelFormSet.model` and `BaseModelFormSet.edit_only` on it (`django/forms/models.py:modelformset_factory`).

`BaseModelFormSet.__init__` keeps `initial=` as `BaseModelFormSet.initial_extra`, the initial values of the extra forms, the first for the first: the initial forms take theirs from their objects (`django/forms/models.py:BaseModelFormSet._construct_form`).

If it is not `QuerySet.totally_ordered`, it is ordered by its own ordering or the model's and then by `"pk"`, so that, a comment says, every formset made from it has its forms in the same order: Ship's ordering by name becomes `"name"` and `"pk"` (`django/forms/models.py:BaseModelFormSet.get_queryset`) ([Annotations, ordering and the other methods that change the query](../querysets/methods.md)).
It is not cut to `BaseFormSet.max_num`; a comment cites ticket 13023, and every existing object is shown (`django/forms/formsets.py:BaseFormSet.total_form_count`).

Unbound, `BaseModelFormSet.initial_form_count` evaluates the queryset to count it, and `_construct_form` gives each form the object at its position (`django/forms/models.py:BaseModelFormSet.initial_form_count`).
It does so for a key that is automatic, not editable, or not among the form's fields (`django/forms/models.py:BaseModelFormSet.add_fields`).

It reads the key from the data, `"form-0-id"`, converts it with the `to_python` of the key's field, or of the field at the end of its relations, and looks it up in a dictionary of the queryset's objects by key (`django/forms/models.py:BaseModelFormSet._existing_object`).
Then the key's field is made required on each initial form, and a form without its key fails (`django/forms/models.py:BaseModelFormSet._construct_form`).
`BaseModelFormSet.clean` calls `BaseModelFormSet.validate_unique`, which compares the forms with one another (`django/forms/models.py:BaseModelFormSet.validate_unique`).
`BaseModelFormSet.save` saves the initial forms' objects, then the extra forms', and returns those it saved (`django/forms/models.py:BaseModelFormSet.save`).

It deletes the object of a form marked for deletion, by `BaseModelFormSet.delete_existing`, and saves a form that has changed, by `BaseModelFormSet.save_existing`; a form that has not changed is not saved (`django/forms/models.py:BaseModelFormSet.save_existing_objects`).

`BaseModelFormSet.save_new_objects` saves, by `BaseModelFormSet.save_new`, each extra form that has changed and is not marked for deletion (`django/forms/models.py:BaseModelFormSet.save_new_objects`).

`inlineformset_factory` calls `modelformset_factory` with `BaseInlineFormSet` as the formset, and sets on the class, as `BaseInlineFormSet.fk`, the foreign key from child to parent (`django/forms/models.py:inlineformset_factory`).

The key is found by `_get_foreign_key`: the field `fk_name=` names, checked, or else the one `ForeignKey` of the child that points at the parent, at an ancestor of it, or at a proxy of either, with a `ValueError` if there is none or several (`django/forms/models.py:_get_foreign_key`).

Where the form's `Meta` lists fields without the foreign key, it adds the key to the list, in the form class's options, with the comment that validation must not be skipped on that field: `_get_validation_exclusions` excludes what the list leaves out (`django/forms/models.py:BaseInlineFormSet.__init__`).
The prefix is the name of the parent's accessor for its children (`django/forms/models.py:BaseInlineFormSet.get_default_prefix`):

`BaseInlineFormSet.add_fields` puts an `InlineForeignKeyField` under the foreign key's name: hidden, not required, and initially the parent's key, or the value of the parent's field the foreign key points at (`django/forms/models.py:BaseInlineFormSet.add_fields`).
It never counts as changed, so an extra form holding only that value is still empty (`django/forms/models.py:InlineForeignKeyField`).

`BaseModelForm._post_clean` leaves an `InlineForeignKeyField` out of the instance's `full_clean`, since, its comment says, the value may not be supplied and the parent may not yet exist (tickets 12507 and 12749), and keeps it in the unique checks (`django/forms/models.py:BaseModelForm._post_clean`).

`BaseInlineFormSet.save_new` sets the parent on each new child again before saving it, since, its comment says, the parent may have been saved after the formset was made (`django/forms/models.py:BaseInlineFormSet.save_new`).

With `save_as_new=True`, `_construct_form` blanks each form's key and foreign key in the data, making a `QueryDict` mutable for the moment, and `BaseInlineFormSet.initial_form_count` answers zero, so every form is an extra form and every child saved is a new object of the formset's parent (`django/forms/models.py:BaseInlineFormSet._construct_form`).
